PullRequest.Title: sessions: dismiss the phone drawer when navigating to a page
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Opening Automations or Session Settings from the phone drawer changes the
underlying page but leaves the drawer covering it.

Close the drawer through the workbench's existing layout/navigation owner when
opening a custom view or a main-group editor. Reselecting a custom view and
opening another editor in an already-visible editor part also dismiss it.
Desktop sidebars, modal groups and suppressed editor restoration are unchanged.

This fixes mobile audit finding F7. It is stacked on **#348979**, whose history
guard makes replacing the drawer with another navigation layer safe while a
browser-history cleanup is pending. The diff against that branch is two files;
retarget to `main` after the prerequisite merges.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp -- compile-client` — passed, zero errors.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/mobileNavigationStack.test.ts --browser chromium` — **179 passed**.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/mobileNavigationStack.test.ts` — **180 passed**.
- `git diff --check` and normal commit hygiene hooks — passed.
- `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" npm run bundle-mobile` — passed
  unchanged policy at `4a92707b8829347e46406f78a81c2261367222b0`.

The two new navigation regressions failed before the fix. Coverage includes
opening/reopening custom views, stale drawer-layer removal, visible/hidden
editors, modal groups, suppressed restoration, desktop sidebars and startup
before the grid exists. Existing navigation-stack and desktop layout tests
also pass. Direct bounded source review found no blocker.

| Measurement (including prerequisite) | gzip bytes | Unchanged limit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Initial | 6,308,558 | 7,000,000 |
| Main JavaScript | 5,702,432 | 6,400,000 |
| CSS | 242,471 | 275,000 |
| Runtime | 14,710,195 | 16,500,000 |
| Extensions | 712,868 | 800,000 |

Manual follow-up: open the phone drawer, choose Automations, reopen the drawer
and choose Automations again, then use Back. Open a session's Settings from its
context menu and confirm the editor is no longer covered.

No live settings were changed. Physical iOS/Safari, screen readers and a
deployed build of this change remain unvalidated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a main-group editor on a phone, with the drawer open or already closed and the editor hidden or already visible.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: editorGroupView.doOpenEditor synchronously fires onWillOpenEditor before proceeding with the editor open. The new handler closes the drawer through setSideBarHidden and removes its navigation entry; an initially hidden editor then follows the existing reveal path. Browser history traversal is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hide the sidebar grid view, hide/detach the active pane composite, update DOM classes, and lay out the existing grid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sidebar transition per open-drawer episode, not per file in a batch once the drawer is closed. Grid leaf geometry caching suppresses downstream layout when dimensions and position do not change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening an eligible editor did not close the drawer on this path; the existing editor reveal still ran when needed. The same close operation already existed for drawer toggles, Back, and other navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded synchronous UI work precedes editor opening. It is the existing drawer-close operation needed to reveal the destination; no collection-wide reconstruction is established.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove the sidebar navigation entry and conditionally call history.back; rearm the single guard with pushState if another layer replaces it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one history cleanup traversal when removing the final layer, followed by at most one guard rearm after a replacement. No history operation for repeated closes with no sidebar entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This editor-open handler did not remove the sidebar entry. The history guard and pending-pop coalescing were already implemented in the base revision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The traversal is asynchronous and is not awaited by editor opening; only bounded stack manipulation and browser API invocation are synchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One handler invocation per eligible editor-open event. For N opens without reopening the drawer, only the first can perform a sidebar visibility transition; later calls return from setSideBarHidden immediately and only check the small navigation-layer stack. The existing main-group lookup scales with main-group count, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI mutations run synchronously on the renderer thread. Multiple opens cannot cause overlapping asynchronous drawer closures. _pendingHistoryPop prevents multiple outstanding history cleanup traversals.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Sidebar visibility acts as an idempotency guard. Drawer closure does not invalidate editor models or recreate the cached pane composite. _savePartVisibility exits immediately on phones, so there is no added persistence serialization or storage write. No new resource cache, miss handling, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the editor event source, suppression/main-group guards, drawer closer, sidebar visibility short circuit, pane-composite hide, grid geometry cache, phone persistence guard, and history synchronization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No device timings are available. Sidebar content complexity and device speed affect one close operation, but the code does not establish a repeated or unbounded regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added work is one necessary, idempotent drawer dismissal per actual visibility transition, with no new filesystem, subprocess, IPC, or network calls established on the added path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, switch, or reselect a custom view from the phone drawer, then close the custom view.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The activeCustomViewOpen autorun invokes _applyCustomViewGridVisibility. When showing a view after grid creation, the new code synchronously closes the drawer before the existing custom-view render/visibility/focus flow. First display retains the existing session-content suspension and grid swap; reselecting uses the existing visibility-equal fast path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Close the drawer using existing pane-composite hiding and grid layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transition for each actual drawer reopening followed by a custom-view open. Subsequent requests with the drawer closed perform no sidebar layout transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Custom-view navigation left the phone drawer open. Rendering, session-content suspension, exclusive-part updates, and final layout already ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the custom-view transition. Geometry caching limits redundant leaf layout; the changed code does not create per-session or per-view fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove the drawer layer and retain or rearm the existing single browser-history guard for the custom-view layer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cleanup traversal plus one rearm when replacing the only drawer layer; no traversal when another tracked layer remains. Reselecting an already tracked custom view does not add another custom-view entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing custom-view layer could be pushed while the sidebar entry remained. The underlying history synchronization implementation is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No awaited history completion blocks rendering. Pending-pop handling preserves bounded synchronization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the selected custom-view identifier through IStorageService before publishing the open request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing logical storage update per showCustomView request; the identifier is a single string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same storage update occurred before the same observable update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing upstream service work; the diff neither adds another write nor changes its scheduling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Instantiate and attach a CustomViewNode when descriptor identity changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One node replacement per changed descriptor, zero replacements for reselecting the same descriptor; unchanged before and after the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same descriptor guard and node creation/disposal behavior applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing custom-view rendering remains on the navigation path, with no newly introduced construction or downstream resource-loading frequency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One call per custom-view open request, not per registered view, session, or sidebar row. Each reopened drawer can cause one close transition. Repeated requests while the drawer stays closed skip sidebar layout work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions and layout updates are synchronous. There is one shared MobileNavigationStack history guard; pending history cleanup is coalesced rather than spawning one traversal per request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CustomViewGridPart.setView compares descriptor identity and does not recreate the node when reselecting the same descriptor. The diff preserves this guard. Phone part-visibility persistence remains disabled. No cache invalidation or new retained collection is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced observable ownership, custom-view visibility branches, descriptor-identity guard, drawer visibility guard, and single-guard history cleanup. Added tests cover opening and reopening.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout duration depends on current content and phone hardware. No concrete repeated heavyweight rendering, new remote boundary, or lifetime growth is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The new call dismisses one existing overlay without defeating renderer reuse or multiplying work by the session/view collection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop navigation, modal/non-main editor opens, suppressed editor restoration, custom-view closure, and custom-view startup before grid creation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Desktop navigation fails the new phone guards. Non-main and suppressed editor opens return before the added close. Custom-view hiding and pre-grid custom-view restoration fail the new visible/grid checks, preserving their previous paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time additional viewport or visibility guard per otherwise eligible call. No newly added work scales with restored editors, session count, or custom-view count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No scheduling, concurrency, or queueing changes on these excluded paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing desktop storage, editor restoration, custom-view descriptor reuse, and startup visibility state are unchanged. No new cache or retained resource.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: directly established by the changed guards, their ordering, surrounding methods, DesktopWorkbench override, and added exclusion tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful magnitude uncertainty for the absence of added expensive-boundary calls on these guarded paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Existing rendering and persistence boundaries are not newly reached by the changed code in these scenarios.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the full two-file inventory and every diff page, tracing navigation ownership, synchronous layout, pane-composite lifecycle, persistence guards, descriptor reuse, and browser-history coalescing. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was established. Review was read-only and static; no findings submitted.
